Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Frogeye leaf spots (small brown circles with purple margins), sunken cankers on limbs, and firm, black decaying rot on the fruit.
treatment: Prune out dead wood, infected branches, and remove mummified fruit during winter dormancy
Apply protective fungicides such as captan or thiophanate-methyl from silver tip through harvest
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Burn or bury pruned debris to destroy spores, protect trees from physical wounds, and maintain optimal tree vigor.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are crisp and consistently green. Fruit skin is smooth and free of lesions or dark spots.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain scheduled pruning, regular watering, and seasonal nutrient management.

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Velvety, olive-green to brown spots on leaves that turn black and puckered; corky, brown, scabby lesions on the fruit skin.
treatment: Apply lime-sulfur or copper fungicides in early spring during the green tip stage
Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering spores
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant scab-resistant apple cultivars and prune the canopy aggressively to maximize sunlight and airflow.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright, striking orange or yellow spots on the upper leaf surface, with tiny tube-like structures releasing spores on the leaf underside.
treatment: Apply systemic fungicides containing myclobutanil or mancozeb as buds begin to open in spring
Hand-pick and destroy orange, gelatinous galls found on nearby juniper/cedar trees
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Avoid planting apple trees within several hundred yards of eastern red cedars or ornamental junipers.
